insights.claim: KubeRay uses a multi-controller architecture where authentication, network isolation, and mTLS are handled by independent controllers watching the same RayCluster CRD, enabling opt-in security features without coupling to the core lifecycle controller.
insights.reasoning: The AuthenticationController, NetworkPolicyController, and RayClusterMTLSController each independently reconcile RayCluster resources. This separation means authentication and network policy can be enabled or disabled per-cluster without modifying the core RayClusterReconciler, reducing coupling and allowing incremental security hardening.

insights.claim: The kube-rbac-proxy sidecar image reference defaults to a hardcoded digest-pinned image and is overridden at runtime via RELATED_IMAGE_ODH_KUBE_RBAC_PROXY_IMAGE, creating an implicit dependency on the RHOAI operator CSV relatedImages for disconnected environment support.
insights.reasoning: In disconnected environments, the default hardcoded image reference will not be resolvable. The operator depends on the ODH/RHOAI operator injecting RELATED_IMAGE_ODH_KUBE_RBAC_PROXY_IMAGE via the CSV. If this env var is missing or the image is not mirrored, RayCluster authentication will fail silently when the sidecar container cannot pull its image.

insights.claim: The operator dynamically reads the OpenShift cluster-wide TLS security profile and watches for changes, restarting itself when the profile is updated, ensuring it tracks the platform crypto policy without manual reconfiguration.
insights.reasoning: The tls-profile-watcher controller watches apiservers.config.openshift.io/cluster and triggers a graceful restart via context cancellation when the TLS profile changes. This is a proactive crypto compliance pattern that avoids operator-TLS-profile drift.
